notes: τὰ τοῦ νηπίου is split three ways: the outer substantival article takes the nominal *things* (rule 22), the inner article is unrepresented for want of any written determiner (rules 23, 57), and the genitive takes the recast attributive *childish*.

Both ὅτε are aligned to whatever introduces their English clause — *When* at the verse head and the two-word *now that* headed on *now*, as rule 61 heads *before that* on *before* — which is rule 24's habit and not two analyses.
The four supplied indefinites before *child* and *man* are rule 7 helpers on their anarthrous nouns, no article standing to compete (rule 51).
Verb-to-verb mapping verified against both Greek and ASV order: ἐφρόνουν takes *felt* and ἐλογιζόμην takes *thought*.
